importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is significant — single cabin vs multi-seat block vs panel-build are immediately distinguishable, and material type (RCC vs FRP/MS) is visually identifiable. Buyers use the image to confirm product type before reading any text; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Seat count, toilet type (Indian/Western), and structure type are primary shortlisting criteria — buyers arrive with a defined project requirement and use specs to confirm fit before any further engagement. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated for government scheme procurement.

Government scheme buyers (SBM, PMAY) have fixed per-unit budgets and actively compare prices across sellers; price varies substantially with seat count and structure type, so buyers discover across configurations rather than arriving with a fixed spec tier. India price sensitivity is high in this segment.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Single-cabin buyers quote per piece; government tenders for multi-seat blocks often quote per seat or per block — this ambiguity creates real price comparison confusion and unit must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Per piece vs per seat vs per block is a genuine market ambiguity in multi-seat procurement; price cannot be meaningfully compared without knowing the unit basis, particularly in bulk government tender contexts.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant brand names exist with buyer recall in RCC toilet cabins; buyers search by spec, price, and compliance track record, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional buyers (gram panchayats, NGOs, PWD) evaluate manufacturer credentials, SBM technical compliance, and past supply experience during vendor selection, but no brand names drive initial search or shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Seat count is the primary product scale separator — a 1-seat cabin and an 8-seat block are non-interchangeable and price scales directly and substantially with seat count, making this the dominant price-driving configurator.

Indian vs Western vs Urinal Block defines what the product IS functionally — these are non-interchangeable configurations for rural vs urban/institutional use, and each commands a distinct price point and buyer segment.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Government tender buyers and institutional procurement specify minimum concrete grade (M30/M35/M40/M45) as a structural compliance requirement under SBM technical specifications and IS 456:2000; sellers need this to confirm structural eligibility and price accordingly.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Seat count directly determines project scale and price — a seller cannot quote accurately or confirm supply capability without knowing whether the buyer needs a single cabin or an 8-seat block.
Indian vs Western vs combined configuration is non-interchangeable for rural vs urban/institutional use; sellers need this to confirm they supply the correct toilet type for the project.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer requires a precast monolithic unit, panel-build site-assembled unit, or cast-in-situ structure to confirm supply capability, determine transport feasibility for remote locations, and price logistics accurately.
